name: János Forgách
summary:
Count János Forgách de Ghymes et Gács was a prominent Austro-Hungarian diplomat of Hungarian origin who played a pivotal role during World War I and the July Crisis.

Born on October 24, 1870, in Halič, Ukraine, Forgách served as the Austrian Ambassador to Italy from 1909 until his death in 1935. He was known for his diplomatic skills and strategic thinking, which helped navigate complex international relationships during a tumultuous period in European history.

Forgách's significance lies in his ability to maintain relations with various nations, including Italy, Germany, and the United Kingdom, despite the rising tensions leading up to the war. His efforts to prevent conflict and promote peace were instrumental in shaping the course of events during the July Crisis.

As a key figure in Austro-Hungarian diplomacy, Forgách's legacy extends beyond his own time, influencing international relations and diplomatic practices for generations to come.

The phrase 'in the shadow of the eagle' ('a gyepen árnyékában') encapsulates Forgách's life and work, symbolizing his dedication to Austria-Hungary's interests despite facing significant challenges from within and outside its borders.
